Statements about Jewish and Christian worship below are attributed to Ibn Zayd in the source, not presented as independently verified historical facts.
translation_en:
Concerning His words, 'For you is your religion, and for me is my religion': God says: Yours is your religion, which you will never abandon, because a seal has been placed upon you and it has been decreed that you will not depart from it and will die adhering to it. Mine is the religion I follow, which I will never abandon, because it has already been established in God's prior knowledge that I will not leave it for another.

Yunus related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Ibn Zayd said concerning God's words, 'For you is your religion, and for me is my religion': This concerns the polytheists. He said: The Jews worship only God and do not associate partners with Him, but they disbelieve in some prophets and in what those prophets brought from God. They disbelieve in God's messenger and in what he brought from God, and they killed groups of prophets unjustly and aggressively. He continued with a statement about the group that remained until Nebuchadnezzar appeared, and their saying 'Uzayr is the son of God.' [The intervening wording in the stored Arabic is unclear and needs checking against an edition.] They did not worship him and did not act as the Christians did, who said 'The Messiah is the son of God' and worshipped him.

Some specialists in Arabic used to say that 'I do not worship what you worship' and the following wording were repeated for emphasis, as in 'Indeed, with hardship comes ease; indeed, with hardship comes ease,' and 'You will surely see Hell; then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty.'

End of the commentary on Surah al-Kafirun.
